name: Alistair Strathmore
source_profile:
[p. 26] Duke Alistair Strathmore demanded an investigation and the withdrawal of the royal commissioners. When these demands were rejected, several northern lords began raising troops to defend their territories. The subsequent escalation from armed resistance to declared secession took place over the following months. The Red Steps were therefore not necessarily the first violent incident in the growing dispute, but they became the symbolic beginning of the civil war.

[p. 26] The event had obvious political ramifications for the realm’s Great Houses. Baron Merrick Rooke refused to relinquish his banner and was killed, becoming an early martyr of the northern cause. House Rooke was stripped of its remaining rights following the rebellion, but its descendants were never entirely extinguished. Sir Oswin Crowthorne commanded the royal soldiers enforcing the decree. His older brother, Alaric, would later become one of the rebellion's most notorious military commanders. Oswin’s responsibility for the bloodshed remains disputed, he remained loyal to the king and ultimately was bestowed his brother's confiscated title of the Earl of Greywatch by King Dedericus IV. Countess Adela Marris was visiting Brackenford at the time as part of a northern noble delegation protesting the late king’s decree. She witnessed the violence and subsequently became a prominent organizer of the northern rebellion. Duke Alistair Strathmore was not present, but was Baron Rooke's overlord as Duke of Orleade. Afterward, he publicly condemned the crown's actions and helped unite the northern houses in opposition.
source_reference: Handbook v0.4, pp. 152–161; Legendarium v1.0, pp. 148–157; project NPC index; Legendarium v1.0 contextual excerpts (page labels included)
